title: Order Our Book! Vintage Watches: The Modern Guide
description: The Modern Guide by Eric Wind and Charlie Dunne of Wind Vintage Following the growth and success of Wind Vintage in selling vintage and pre-owned modern watches and designing sell-out watch collaborations, Eric Wind has teamed with his colleague Charlie Dunne, Vice President of Wind Vintage, to write Vintage Watches: The Modern Guide published by Ten Speed Press of Penguin Random House. James Fisk provided all the photography. The book is 320 pages in length and features over 250 photographs. The book launches for sale on November 17 at all major book sellers. The book features personal essays by many notable watch collectors including David Chang, Ben Clymer, Ronny Chieng, Brad Faxon, Gary Shteyngart, Aly & AJ Michalka, and more. “It has been a dream come writing a book about my passion: vintage watches," said Eric Wind, Founder of Wind Vintage. “Our goal was to make a book that would help those interested in watches to learn more about them while also remaining relevant and educational for the most sophisticated collectors.” “Writing this book has been an amazing experience. It is filled with incredible vintage watches Eric and I both love and would be thrilled to own,” said Charlie Dunne, Vice President and Senior Watch Specialist of Wind Vintage. “There are so many grail watches throughout the book and we are thrilled to share our passion with current and future watch collectors.” “It has been a great pleasure to visit my friends at Wind Vintage in Palm Beach so many times over the last few years and shoot so many wonderful vintage watches,” said James Fisk, the photographer for the book. “To see these photographs collected in a beautifully printed book is especially meaningful, and I hope readers will find the same joy in discovering the beauty and character of vintage watches that I have found in photographing them.” Vintage Watches: The Modern Guide retails for $60 USD and can be pre-ordered for $50 USD on Amazon.com to arrive on launch day: Tuesday, November

title: Breguet Tourbillon Reference 3357 in 18K White Gold Unpolished
description: The Breguet Tourbillon 3357 is the direct successor to the 3350, which was not only the first wristwatch Tourbillon from Breguet - the brand that invented the Tourbillon - but also the last watch developed by legendary watchmaker Daniel Roth during his time at the manufacturer. The watch is powered by the calibre 558.1 manual wind tourbillon. The calibre was developed by Lemania, and is among the most lavishly hand decorated movements of the era. The case features the traditional cold rolled and fluted case, with its distinctive welded lugs in the ‘Breguet Empire’ style. The 3357 was introduced in the mid 1990s to roll out a host of updates to the original watch, most notably the Cal. 558.1. This particular example dates to 2007. While these were offered in both yellow and rose gold, white metals like platinum and the present white gold are considerably rarer and seldom seen offered. The case diameter is 36mm, and the case appears to be unpolished with all hallmarks present and accounted for. Fitted to a period Breguet deployant clasp, the watch presents extremely well. It is paired on a Breguet deployant buckle. This example features a Z serial dating to circa 2007. The watch does not come with box and papers. We do not know the service history, but it is running well.

title: Rolex Day-Date Champagne Dial Reference 18038 in 18K YG Unpolished
description: The legendary Rolex Day-Date was introduced in 1956 and was the first timepiece to feature both the date and the full day of the week spelled out. The Day-Date reference 18038 was introduced in circa 1878. The watch is an iconic watch that is one of the most recognizable timepieces on the planet. This Rolex Day-Date reference 18038 is a phenomenal example. The 18K yellow gold case appears to be unpolished. It measures 36mm in diameter. The watch features an outstanding champagne dial - one of the most recognized and respected variants of the Day-Date. It features a 9.3M serial dating to circa 1986-1987. The watch does not come with box and papers. We do not know the service history, but it is running great. It recently passed a water resistance test of 5 bar.

title: Rolex Oyster Perpetual Reference 67198 in 18k YG Unpolished w/ Papers
description: This Rolex Oyster Perpetual reference 67198 is an incredbile special ladies Oyster Perpetual that measures approximately 26mm in diameter. These yellow gold OPs are some of the most attractive ladies Rolex models - perhaps some of the coolest watches from the manufacturer. I love the champagne dials - particularly when they have warm tones like the present example. The case appears to be unpolished and has beautiful finishing on the lugs. The watch is paired on the impossible to find Rolex Rivet 7204A bracelet. The watch dates to circa 1997 and features an U4 serial. It comes with Japanese papers indicating the watch was sold in 2003. This is the perfect watch to buy for your woman of your dreams because you would be in love with a woman wearing one of the sickest OPs on the planet and talk to her about it everyday. The watch does not come with box, but comes with papers. We do not know the service history of this watch, but it is running well. It recently passed a water resistance test of 5 bar.

title: F.P.Journe Chronomètre À Résonance Ref. RN Souveraine Platinum Grey Dial Full Set Unpolished
description: The Chronomètre à Résonance is arguably his most iconic model. François-Paul Journe took inspiration for the Chronomètre À Résonance from pendulum clocks featuring two complete movements and independent precision escapements. Each of these pendulums exchanged energy with a synchronized natural resonance, neutralizing external vibrations. The power reserve indicator is located at twelve o’clock and uses the format seen in marine chronometers. This is an early 2nd generation example of the RN (Resonance Nouvelle) in platinum sold in 2005. The watch is powered by the rare 18k rose gold calibre 1499.2. The rose gold calibre 1499.2 was produced for a short period after Journe transitioned from the rhodium-plated brass movement. These are seen from circa 2005-2006. Soon after, the 1499.2 was replaced by the calibre 1499.3. This Chronomètre à Résonance reference RN is made of platinum. It measures 40mm in diameter. The case appears to be unpolished. The dial is made of white gold. It is a stunning and clean look against the platinum case. It is paired on an original F.P.Journe leather strap and platinum buckle. The Chronomètre À Résonance reference RN would remain in production until 2009 and remains an icon in independent watchmaking and one of the most desirable wristwatches on the planet. We do not know the service history, but the watch is running well. It comes full set with a box and card.

title: Audemars Piguet Complete Calendar in 18K Yellow Gold Unpolished
description: The Archives This Audemars Piguet Complete Calendar wristwatch is one of the most sophisticated wristwatches produced in the early 20th century. By the early 1930s, wristwatches began to take center stage and were being produced at higher percentages than pocket watches. This Audemars Piguet’s movement dates to circa 1927 making it one of the earliest complicated wristwatches from an era where most timepieces coming out of Switzerland were pocket watches. This example would have been among the most complicated timepieces produced for a wristwatch during the period. The watch measures approximately 25mm in diameter by 37mm in length. The case is described as “pale” yellow gold. The case back features a cursive hand engraving that reads “My Dearest, Remember me always. Your loving Celine Dec 2nd, 1942”. These movements would have been incredibly expensive, so it certainly is possible that the watch was produced and sold sometime after the 1930s. The 18k yellow gold has taken on an incredible patina throughout the surfaces. It features applied Breguet numerals and cathedral hands which are very bold on the rectangular dial. The watch is powered by the calibre 10GHSM - a complete calendar movement highlighting the day, date, month, and moon phases. These movements were introduced in the early 1920s and were among the most sophisticated and complicated calibres offered. It is believed that only 48 examples of the rectangular/tank models were produced. In “pale” yellow, it is estimated 35 were produced. Less than a dozen are known publicly. Many feature different dial variants. Some of these examples can be seen at auction and in books covering Audemars Piguet. This example was sold in 2025 at Christie’s . A similar example in platinum was just sold at Monaco Legends Auctions for $816,360 It was just serviced and is running well. It does not come with a box or papers.

title: Daniel Roth Papillon 10th Anniversary Limited Edition in 18K White Gold
description: The final timepiece created by Daniel Roth was the Papillon line, which was introduced in 1998 to commemorate the 10th anniversary of the brand. This example is produced in 18k white gold. The Papillon 10th Anniversary was produced 250 examples across three metals. The white gold variant consists of 110 examples. This dial is an incredibly beautiful guilloche with alternating patterns. The Papillon was Roth’s first wristwatch to incorporate a jumping hour and retrograde minutes. This example dates to circa 1999. It is powered by the automatic modified Girard-Perregaux calibre 3000. The watch measures 35mm in diameter by 41mm lug to lug. For those who admire the incredible jump-hour wristwatches, this is a grail timepiece. The watch was just serviced and is running well. It does not come with a box or papers.

title: Berneron Mirage 38 Prussian Blue In 18K Full Set Unpolished
description: The Berneron Mirage debuted in 2023. This asymetrical model made an incredible impression with collectors and is synonymous with the brand. The Mirage 34 is the is the smaller iteration of the Mirage series whereas the 38 is the larger model. The Prussian Blue is a special configuration introduced in 2024. It is a rare and highly desirable Berneron Mirage model. These watches are powered by the in-house calibre 233 which is beautifully displayed through the exhibition case back. The movement’s mainplate and bridges are made of 18k gold. It is a manual-wind movement with a 72 hour power reserve. It features curved white gold hands to complement the asymmetrical case. The case measures 38mm × 34mm x 7mm and is made of 18k white gold. It measures 42mm lug to lug. This example is unpolished and remains in outstanding condition. It is paired on the original strap and buckle. For those who admire the independent watchmaking spirit, Berneron is certainly the most exciting manufacturer that has emerged in the 2020s. The Prussian Blue has had incredible results recently selling for over $390,000. The "Viridian" Chrysoprase models have also had great results recently selling at $521,400 on LoupeThis and $497,000 at Phillips. The watch is running well. It comes full set with a box and papers from the original owner.

title: Cartier $20 Double Eagle Coin Watch Unpolished
description: This example is an exceptional 1898 $20 Double Eagle $20 coin. These are the ultimate horological accessories and, in our view, way cooler than any Cartier timepiece that you could purchase today. With the prices being purchased on brand new Cartier Crashes, a very nice Cartier coin watch should be +$50,000! The watch is engraved beautifully with initials - perhaps from an individual that gave the watch to their friend. The interior is also engraved with 'vouloir c'est pouvoir' - “where there’s a will, there’s a way”. We believe the watch dates to circa 1927 - and could likely be older than Henry Graves Jr.’s Patek Philippe coin watch. It is very similar to the Babe Ruth coin Eric sold at Christie’s in 1926 that was “given” to New York gangster "Bumpy” Johnson . We do not know the service history, but it is running great. It does not come with box or papers. It does come with a blue box that is likely not original to the watch and two small pouches that these coin watches were often sold with. To learn more about vintage coin watches read Charlie Dunne’s authoritative article 'An introduction to coin watches: Where craftsmanship meets currency' ! Charlie Dunne is really awesome!

title: Joe DiMaggio's Patek Philippe Breguet Dial Reference 130 Chronograph in 18K YG w/ Extract
description: This remains the longest consecutive-game hitting streak in MLB history to this day! Throughout the May 15 to July 16, 1941 streak, he batted .408 with 15 home runs and 55 RBIs. Joltin’ Joe’s career started alongside the “Iron Horse” Lou Gehrig and ended alongside Micky Mantle. He operated at the intersection of two legendary Yankees eras (with Gehrig who played alongside Babe Ruth and was part of the Murderers’ Row 1927 Yankees team) and then with Mantle who of course had the legendary home run duel with his teammate Roger Maris in 1961. From 1943–1945, DiMaggio served in the U.S. Army Air Forces during World War II (which many cite as his prime years). DiMaggio had a lifetime batting average of .325 and accumulated 361 home runs. In 1955, DiMaggio was elected into the National Baseball Hall of Fame. In 1969, Joe DiMaggio was voted the greatest living baseball player. He famously married Marilyn Monroe in 1954 and they had a short marriage, but they rekindled their relationship years later and were reportedly close to marrying again before Monroe passed in 1962. According to the Extract from the Archives, this timepiece was produced in 1947 and was sold on December 12, 1948. The dial features beautiful hand-cut Breguet numerals which are confirmed in the Extract notes. It features the tachymeter scale demarcated for miles on the perimeter of the dial. This example features the spade hand configuration which was popular in the American market during the late 1940s. The watch is powered by the prestigious calibre 13-130 which was featured in many of the most important chronographs from Patek Philippe in this period. The case measures 33mm in diameter, and wears large at 41mm lug-to-lug. The 18k yellow gold case was produced by Emile Vichet, the Geneva master casemaker and features the Poinçon de Maître number 9. (Stainless steel reference 130s were produced by Wenger, Crossier or Dubois.) Emile Vichet produced the gold cases for the legendary Patek Philippe reference

title: Patek Philippe Aquanaut Ref 5164A-001 Khaki Green Strap Box & Papers Unpolished
description: This Patek Philippe Aquanaut reference 5164A is a spectacular complicated sports watch from the leading name in watchmaking. The travel-time complication is powered by the calibre 324 S C FUS allowing the owner to simplify a second reference time while away from home. The case is made of stainless steel. It appears to be unpolished. It measures approximately 41mm in diameter. This example was sold in 2019. The watch is paired on the iconic Khaki green rubber strap which sell for $8,000! The watch will fit a wrist over 7 inches. It comes from the original owner. Good provenance. This watch comes with box and papers. The outer cloth for the box is missing. The watch pillow for the interior box is missing. We do not know the service history but it is running well.

title: Patek Philippe Black Dial Chronograph Reference 5170G-010 Retailed by Tiffany & Co. Full Set Unpolished
description: This Patek Philippe chronograph reference 5170G-010 is a spectacular white gold timepiece with white gold Breguet numerals and a black double-signed dial from prestigious New York retailer Tiffany & Co. This is the most coveted and rare configuration of the reference 5170G. There are reportedly only 12 black dial examples of the 5170G that were ever stamped Tiffany & Co. Ben Clymer famously has one of them. Kevin Rose was an original owner of another, and rumor has it that John Mayer has one in his world-class Patek collection as well. We believe that the dial and case combination of these few pieces make them the most attractive modern Patek Philippe chronographs, by far. The reference 5170 chronograph is powered by the famous Patek calibre CH 29-535 PS movement, the company’s first fully in-house manually wound chronograph movement. The exhibition sapphire back leaves this gorgeous movement on full display. The black dial and Breguet numerals on these pieces are just breathtaking. The case measures approximately 39mm in diameter and 47mm lug to lug. We do not know the service history, but the watch is running well. Rarer these days, this grail piece comes as a proper full set with its original Patek and Tiffany’s boxes, its papers, black leather strap and white gold deployant buckle along with an extra Patek Philippe black leather strap, also from Tiffany & Co. The watch comes from the original owner who purchased the watch in 2018 from Tiffany & Co. in New York City.

title: Patek Philippe Nautilus 5980/60G-001 Flyback Chronograph in 18k WG Unpolished Full Set
description: This Patek Philippe Nautilus reference 5980/60G-001 is one of the most desirable Patek Philippe wristwatches. The Patek Philippe Nautilus reference 5980/60G-001 was introduced in April 2024. It is cherished by collectors for the sporty style and casual look. This watch is a fantastic Nautilus with flyback chronograph movement. The watch is powered by the automatic calibre CH 28-520 C. The 18k white gold case measures 40.5mm in diameter. The case is unpolished. It is comes with the original calfskin denim pattern strap and also comes wth the additional original fabric pattern, blue-gray. The watch is paired on the original 18k white gold deployant buckle. The watch was sold in 2026 and is in outstanding condition. The watch comes “full set” with box and the Certificate of Origin and pin pusher. The watch is running well and keeping great time.

title: Patek Philippe Amagnetic Reference 3417 w/ Service Papers & Extract
description: The Patek Philippe reference 3417 is an iconic model with a very interesting role in the manufacturer’s history. The 3417 was introduced in 1958 and remained in production into the late 1960s. While many antimagnetic timepieces were being produced - the likes of the Railmaster, Milgauss, Ingenieur - Patek Philippe created a refined offering for the professional. This example features a patinated dial. The case has been polished, but it is attractive. The watch measures 35mm in diameter (43mm lug-to-lug). It is powered by the calibre 27-AM 400. This watch does not include the original box and papers. It comes with the Patek Philippe Extract from the Archives and was produced and sold in 1962. The watch has just arrived back from Patek Geneva with an overhaul and restoration. It has remained unworn since the return. It comes with Patek Philippe service papers from November 2026 and is running well. The Extract indicates that “the original case was replaced by the actual - bearing the number 2.627.966 - during a servicing in 1963.”

title: Patek Philippe Blue Dial Reference 5270G-019 in 18K WG Full Set Unpolished
description: The Patek Philippe reference 5270 is a remarkable grand complication model introduced by Patek Philippe in 2011. It is one of the most desirable and appreciated manual-winding perpetual calendar chronograph models produced by the manufacturer. The watch powered by the calibre CH 29-535 PS Q. This example features an 18K white gold case with beautiful blue dial with tachymeter scale. The case measures 41mm in diameter. It features applied markers with leaf hands. The lugs design and stepped edges make for one of the most interesting case designs in the catalog. The case appears to be unpolished. It is one of the most enjoyable models from their catalog to wear. It is accompanied by an exhibition case back and a white gold case back. The watch is paired on the original Patek Philippe leather strap and deployant. The watch comes full set with box and and Certificate of Origin. It was sold in 2016. We do not know the service history but is is running well.

title: Patek Philippe Reference 5396G-014 in 18K WG Full Set Unpolished
description: This is a very special Patek Philippe reference 5396G. The watch is powered by the calibre 324 S QA LU 24H, an automatic annual calendar. This dial variant is among my personal favorites featuring a grey soleil finish and applied-Breguet numerals. The watch is in fantastic condition. The case appease to be unpolished. The white-gold case wears incredible on the wrist. It measures 38.5mm in diameter (48mm lug-to-lug). The watch comes full set with box and papers. It comes with the pin pusher and hang tag. The Certificate of Origin does not feature a date of sale. We do now know the service history but it is running well.

title: Patek Philippe Heures Sautantes Diamond Set Reference 3619/3 in 18K White Gold Unpolished w/ Extract
description: This is an incredibly special and possibly unique Patek Philippe referece 3619/3 in 18k white gold. The watch is fresh to market from the family of the original owner. The original owner purchased the watch from Patek Philippe in the 1970s and was a successful New York based attorney. It is massive case measuring 40mm in diameter by 35mm in length. The bracelet is an intricately woven white gold design that is extremely comfortable on the wrist. The watch will fit a wrist approximately 7.5 inches. These cases were produced by Ateliers Réunis. This particular example appears to be a specially requested example with the unseen diamond bezel. It features 50 brilliant diamonds throughout the bezel and 12 diamond hour markers on the dial. The dial features an indentation between 11 and 12 o’clock. The watch is powered by the “Heures Sautantes” (Jumping Hours) manual-wind calibre 27 HS 400. This imporant calibre also used in the iconic Patek Philippe Travel Time reference 2597. In 1959 this movement was introduced by Patek Philippe through the Swiss Patent 340,191 and was based on a 1953 prototype wristwatch from Louis Cottier. These case profile features two adjustments for setting the travel time forward or backward. The watch was found with the travel time set to the local time concealing the third hand. When the son of the original owner was informed of this important complication they were astonished. These timepieces are incredibly rare. It is estimated that 32 examples of the reference 3619 were made with only 13 examples sold publicly. Many were made with leather straps, and others with integrated bracelets. Dials often feature “ribbon” diamond hour markers for black dials and satiné blue dials will feature the more traditional single diamond hour markers. One example in white gold with white lacquered dial with Breguet numerals on leather strap sold in May of 2026 for approximately $447,000 . title: Patek Philippe Nautilus Reference 3711/1G in 18k White Gold w/ Box & Extract
description: The Patek Philippe Nautilus is perhaps the most desired watch on the planet. The introduction of the model marked the first true sports watch from the manufacturer in 1976. Along with the Audemars Piguet Royal Oak, it ushered in the world of integrated stainless steel watches which are adored by watch enthusiasts today. This Patek Philippe Nautilus is a very special and rare reference 3711/1 in 18k white gold. It is believed 700 examples were produced. The 3711/1G was the successor reference to the 3700/1A. Lord David Snowdon famously wore one for years that was sold at Christie’s. The case is a “Jumbo” and measures 42mm in diameter. It has been lightly polished but is attractive. The reference 3711 was introduced in circa 2004 and was only produced until 2006. This is example dates to 2005. The watch is powered by the calibre 315 SC. It features a beautiful black dial. The 3711 is certainly one of the most attractive iterations of the Nautilus and this is an outstanding example. The watch comes with box. It comes with an Extract from the Archives. We do not know the service history, but it is running well.

title: Patek Philippe Retailed by Brock & Co. Reference 42 Tank in 18K White Gold w/ Extract
description: This is an incredibly special rectangular timepiece from Patek Philippe dating to 1927. The watch is an early wristwatch produced in a time when the primary exports in Switzerland were pocket watches. The wristwatch would eventually become more prominent for Patek Philippe by the early 1930s. This example is a very rare model that was produced for the Beverly Hills based retailer Brock & Co. There are a handful of Patek Philippe wristwatches for Brock & Co of this era. Examples from this period include the references 42 and 425 made of gold or platinum. The designs of these watches were reminiscent of the trend-setting Cartier Tank. The Tank had been released about decade prior, and the Art Deco styles defined the watch industry throughout the 1920s. The dial features an incredible two-tone sector dial with the “Cat Whiskers” hour markers (2, 4, 8, and 9 o’clock). Both the manufactuer and retailer signature are engraved hard enamel. The case is made of 18k white gold. It measures approximately 33mm in length by 25mm in diameter. It has been lightly polished. The case design is quite incredible, as it is reminiscent of the pocket watches and features a hinged case at 12 o’clock. The watch is powered by the manual wind calibre 9 movement with lever escapement. We do not know the service history, but the watch is running well. It does not come with a box or papers. The watch comes with an Extract from the Archives.

title: Patek Philippe Annual Calendar  5205G-013 in 18K WG Service Sealed w/ Copy of Service Papers
description: This Patek Philippe Annual Calendar is a handsome modern calendar watch by one of watchmaking's most historically significant manufacturers. The 18 white gold case measures 40mm in diameter and is 11.36mm thick. It is paired with a black Patek Philippe leather strap. It comes with an 18k white gold Patek Philippe buckle. The watch features a blue dial with apertures for the day, date and month, as well as a moonphase at 6 o'clock. It comes with a solid caseback and does not come with an exhibition case back. The watch was serviced by Patek Philippe in 2022. It comes with a digital copy of service papers and is still sealed. The watch does not come with box and papers. We do not know the date of production.

title: Spencer Tracy's Rolex Explorer Reference 6350 w/ Waffle Dial Unpolished
description: This Rolex Explorer reference 6350 is an incredibly rare and important example from the early 1950s which belonged to American actor Spencer Tracy. This watch was worn in the 1956 movie ‘The Mountain’, an adventure film starring Spencer Tracy and Robert Wagner based on the French novel La neige en deuil. It is possibly one of the earliest product placements of a Rolex in a film. This example features an outstanding black “honeycomb” or “waffle” dial with very attractive lume. The textured Rolex dials of the 1950s are very uncommon and particularly important on Rolex sports models! It is paired on a Rolex Oyster Rivet bracelet with 64 end links dating to 1957 which we added and is period correct. The watch also comes with a Rolex strap and steel buckle which was worn on the Explorer for many years by Tracy. Linked here is a photo of Tracy wearing the watch. This example dates to circa 1953 with a 955,XXX serial It measures 36mm in diameter. The case appears to be unpolished. I’m often asked about which watches I would love to own if I could have anything. Watches like this waffle-dial Rolex Explorer 6350 is at the top of the list and the added provenance is an incredible bonus. This watch certainly belongs in the Rolex Museum collection - as it is the best of the best! To learn more about the history and evolution of the Rolex Explorer I, you can see my video and corresponding article Reference Points A Comprehensive Collector's Guide To The Rolex Explorer I . This watch does not come with box and papers. We do not know the service history but it is running well.

title: Rolex Small Crown Submariner Reference 6536-1 Unpolished
description: The Rolex “Small Crown” Submariner reference 6536 is a classic reference and one of the iconic dive watches. I purchased this watch in 2020 from the sons of the original owner, Louis “Lou” Ross, who led a distinguished career of public service including as an aide to President Kennedy. Lou served as a Foreign Service Officer and wore this Submariner while posted around the world. When he retired, he put the watch away and his sons only recently found it after their mother passed. Amazingly, it seemed that the watch had not been opened since it left Rolex in 1957 and it remains all original including the crystal with slight crazing and original bracelet. Lou’s story is definitely worth telling in greater detail in the future, he was orphaned at age 3 and went on to record the Nuremberg trials as a very young man for the U.S. Government before embarking on a career of public service at important posts around the world, but given all the current interest in Submariners I felt it would be worth showing one of the great ones. The case measures 38mm in diameter (48mm lug-to-lug). The case appears to be unpolished. These models wear very nice on the wrist and are extremely this and light. It features the original “no hash” bezel which is original for pre-1957 and early 1957 Submariners. It was serviced for the first and only time in 2020. The luminous-hour markers have a warm patina which is much more beautiful in person. Complementing the warm lume is the awesome gilt font and chapter ring. The watch dates to circa 1957 and has a 230,XXX serial. It is paired on the original Rolex stretch Rivet bracelet dated to 1957. This watch should be in the Rolex Museum! To learn more about the Rolex Submariner, you can read my ‘ Reference Points: Understanding The Rolex Submariner ’ article and corresponding video. The watch does not come with box and papers. We do not know the service history, but it is running well.

title: Rolex Daytona in Platinum Ice Blue Dial Reference 116506 in Platinum Full Set Unpolished
description: This was the first Daytona to be produced with a platinum case and bracelet. It ushered in the ice-blue dial which collectors love. It is without a doubt a statement timepiece. It takes the iconic sports watch line in an ultra-luxurious direction, which has captured the attention of watch lovers who appreciate the flashier side of Rolex. It is powered by the calibre 4130. This example features a card with the name “Kevin Hart” who we presume to be the legendary comedian and actor. The watch was sold to a collector and was stated it formerly belonged to the comedian. Hart is one of the most successful comedians of all time based on his unrivaled output of blockbuster films and stand up performances. However, Hart is one of the most important watch collectors and tastemakers in the entertainment industry. Charlie Dunne is a big fan of Kevin Hart going back to the early 2000s when he performed on Comedy Central’s talk show Tough Crowd with Colin Quinn (in addition to his 2021 Netflix miniseries True Story ). The watch features his name on the card. It is from the debut year and was originally sold in 2013. The watch measures 40mm in diameter. The case appears to be unpolished. For those who appreciate the platinum Ice Blue Rolex Daytona and admire the comedy mogul, this is an outstanding choice! The watch comes full set with box and papers. It recently passed a water resistance test of 5 bar. We do not know the service history but it is running well.

title: Rolex Zenith Black Dial Daytona Reference 16520 Unpolished
description: The Rolex Zenith Daytona reference 16520 is an outstanding stainless steel sports chronograph. It features a U serial number, which dates to circa 1997. It is paired with a reference 78390 Oyster bracelet with a Z clasp code dating to circa 1997. The case appears to be unpolished. It measures 40mm in diameter. This example features a black dial with tritium luminous material. The watch does not come with a box or papers. We do not know the service history, but the watch is running well. It recently passed a water resistance test of 5 bar.

title: Rolex GMT-Master Ref 1675
description: The Rolex GMT-Master was originally designed for Pan Am pilots in the 1950s and continues to be a flagship model for Rolex to this day. The reference 1675 was introduced in 1959 and remained in production until 1980. This is a super attractive example. The watch has an 1.68M serial dating to circa 1967. It features an attractive faded insert. The zinc sulfide lume is beautiful color. It features the small triangle GMT hand. The case has been polished. The watch is 40mm in diameter (46.5mm lug-to-lug). It is paired on a Rolex 7206 bracelet with solid links and 58 end links with date code dating to 1967. To learn more about the Rolex GMT-Master, you can watch my ‘ Reference Points: Understanding The Rolex GMT-Master ' video and read the corresponding article. You can also read Charlie Dunne’s comprehensive article ‘ Collector's Guide: The Rolex GMT-Master Reference 1675 In Steel ’. The watch does not come with box and papers. We do not know the service history, but it is running well. It recently passed a water resistance test of 5 bar.

title: Rolex GMT-Master Reference 6542 Bakelite Bezel
description: The Rolex GMT-Master reference 6542 marked the first reference in what would go onto become one of the most celebrated timepieces across all manufacturers. The timepiece became an icon within the James Bond movie Goldfinger after being worn by Honor Blackman during her portrayal of "Pussy Galore". It is an unmistakable watch and it is seen as grail watches for collectors who understand the importance of the 1950s Rolex sports catalog. This particular example is an outstanding 6542 with a spectacular dial, vivid original Bakelite bezel, and great provenance. These Bakelite bezels have a propensity for cracks and are radioactive, and as a result many were replaced with non-luminous, anodized aluminum bezels. The colors are so unique and it makes for an out of this world aesthetic. In addition to the Bakelite bezel, the dial is very well preserved and attractive. The reference 6542 dials are often known for cracking and crazing, but this example has one of the nicest dial we have seen on any reference 6542. The GMT hand has minimal lume loss, but this is expected in a sports watch over 65 years old. The case has been lightly polished, but is very attractive and full. The watch has a 398,XXX serial dating to circa late 1958. It is 38mm in diameter (48mm lug-to-lug). It is paired on what is likely its original Swiss-made Oyster rivet bracelet with super-desirable “Big Logo” clasp and 65 end links dating to 1959. It has been in an important private collection for a number of years. We do not know the service history, but it is running well. The watch recently passed a water resistance test of 3 bar. To learn more about the Rolex GMT-Master, you can watch my ‘Reference Points: Understanding The Rolex GMT-Master' video and read the corresponding article. I selected this exact watch for inclusion in the Reference Points article and video, so that should tell you how I feel about the quality of this example.

It is said that Gérald Genta possibly designed these watches and they certainly seemed to be part of the evolution of integrated watch design that led to the Audemars Piguet Royal Oak, IWC Ingenieur 1832, and Patek Philippe Nautilus. This Rolex Cellini King Midas reference 4312 is a special timepiece in 18k yellow gold. The case is unpolished. It measures approximately 24mm in diameter. title: Rolex Tropical Double Red Sea-Dweller Reference 1665 Thin Case
description: This Rolex Sea-Dweller reference 1665 features the highly desired and vibrant "Double Red" dial and the rare thin case. The earliest Sea-Dwellers such as this example used cases like on the Rolex Submariner reference 5512, but with a helium escape valve (HEV) added to the left side of the case. The case is lightly polished, but in strong condition overall. The watch measures 40mm in diameter. It previously came from the original owner. The amazing tropical dial has the original tritium lume on the dial and hands. The aluminum bezel insert has faded to a beautiful grey color. The watch features a 1.7 million serial with inside case back dating to circa 1967. These were not assembled by Rolex to be Sea-Dwellers until later. The watch came from the original owner who purchased it new in New Zealand in the early 1970s. The gentleman’s wife was upset about the cost of the watch, but it was already purchased. The gentleman was a roofer and did various forms of manual labor. One day, he was on a roof and he took his watch off and left it on the roof so it would not get damaged while he was working. Unfortunately, he slipped and fell off the roof. He went to the hospital for a few days and when he regained his senses he realized his Rolex was probably still on the roof. He went back about a week later once he had left the hospital and promptly climbed onto the roof to find his watch still sitting there. He joked that spending the week in the sun up on the roof might have helped the dial turn “tropical” brown. The watch does not come with box and papers. Overall, this is an amazing opportunity to get a spectacular and rare Rolex sports watch. We do not know the service history, but it is running well. title: Tornek-Rayville by Blancpain Reference TR-900 Unpolished
description: The Tornek Rayville reference TR-900 by Blancpain is an iconic dive watch made for the U.S. Navy in the 1960s. These are incredibly rare and highly-coveted versions of the Fifty Fathoms with a great story. These watches were sold by Blancpain under the “Tornek-Rayville” name during the 1960s as a way to be supportive of the “Buy American Act “by way of Blancpain’s United States distributor Allen Tornek. They used the word “Rayville” as an English take on Blancpain’s associated history with the Swiss village Villeret. These watches were introduced in 1964, There were a purported 780 delivered to the United States in that first year. Another 300 examples were purportedly delivered in 1966 - this example coming from the later batch. In the 1970s, the U.S. government destroyed the majority of these watches. It is estimated that fewer than 100 examples still exist. This example is quite cool for anyone who has a penchant for the Rolex Explorer I as it features the case back serial 1016. The sandblasted stainless steel case measures 41mm in diameter. It has come to our attention that the springbars were later reapplied with the current fixed springbars. The hands have been relumed due to previous cracking / fissures. These watches feature the unique humidity indicator on the dials that would alert the wearer if humidity or water were to enter the watch. The watch is powered by the automatic A. Schild calibre 1361. The bezels of these watches are often susceptible to cracking. This example is intact and extremely attractive. We do not know the service history, but the watch is running well. It does not come with box or papers, which is of course to be expected for a U.S.-military issued watch.

The watch features the “AUF / AB" (Up / Down) power-reserve indicator at 8 o’clock. The 18k rose gold case is 39mm in diameter (45.5mm lug-to-lug) and appears to be unpolished. The watch dates to circa 2023. The watch comes full set with box and papers. We do not know the service history but it is running well.

title: Vacheron Constantin Overseas Black Dial 4520V/210A-B483 Unpolished Full Set
description: This Vacheron Constantin Overseas reference 4520V/210A-B483 is a great modern sports watch from one of the most renowned and historically significant manufacturers. The Overseas is considered one of the best luxury sports watches on the planet. The case and bracelet are made of stainless steel. The watch is in excellent condition and appears to be unpolished with minor signs of wear. The watch is powered by the in-house Caliber 5100. The case measures 41mm in diameter. It is paired on the stainless steel integrated bracelet and it comes with a leather and rubber strap from Vacheron Constantin. The watch comes as a “full set” with a box and papers, and is from the original owner. The watch was originally sold in 2025.

title: Vacheron Constantin Historiques Américan 1921 Reference 1100S/00R-H115 in 18k RG Unpolished Full Set
description: This Vacheron Constantin 1921 Historiques Américan is an amazing model. It is a reference 1100S/00R-H115. The case is made of 18k rose gold. The case appears to be unpolished. It measures 36.6mm in diameter. This watch dates to 2026. It is paired on a Vacheron Constantin leather strap and pink gold buckle that was produced Unroc (Cornu)! Cornu & Cie produced buckles for everyone and when I showed this to @WatchAbbie she laughed hysterically. It comes with box and papers. We do not know the service history, but it is running well.

title: Vacheron & Constantin Reference 6908 in 18k YG Unpolished
description: This Vacheron & Constantin reference 6908 is a spectacular timepiece with a bark-like textured case. The 18K yellow gold exterior is made by Wenger. The dimensions measure 26.5mm x 26.5mm. The bracelet should fit a wrist up to 6 inches. The buckle features a pronounced Maltese cross. The watch is powered by the manual wind calibre 1003. The watch does not come with box and papers. We do not know the service history but it is running well and keeping great time..

title: Vacheron Constantin Overseas Reference 42542/423A-8930 Mid-Size Unpolished
description: The Overseas line has recently seen a great deal of appreciation by collectors, and I am proud to offer this example that highlights the heritage of the iconic watch model. This Vacheron Constantin is the younger sibling of the integrated sports model, reference 222. It is the mid-size case. The watch features a white dial with diamond hour markers as well as a diamond set bezel. The stainless steel case measures 37mm in diameter (40mm including the crown). The watch fits a wrist approximately 7 inches. The case appears to be unpolished. The watch does not come with box or papers. We do not know the service history, but it is running well.

title: Audemars Piguet Royal Oak Two-Tone “Jumbo” Reference 5402SA Unpolished
description: A Unpolished The Audemars Piguet Royal Oak is an icon. It is the original luxury sports watch that created and defined the category. Introduced at BaselWorld in 1972 after being designed by Gérald Genta, it turned the Swiss industry upside down and changed the fortunes of the struggling Audemars Piguet. It’s no surprise, that Patek Philippe hired Gerald Genta a few years later to introduce their own version of a steel luxury sports watch: the Nautilus. The dial is in excellent condition, which is uncommon for these. Often these dials can have an uneven and sometimes unattractive patina. This watch features a Montre bracelet with an “Audemars Piguet” flip clasp. The case measures 39mm in diameter (48mm lug to lug) and this is the original “Jumbo”. The case and bracelet appear to be unpolished. The hands appear to be replaced and glow differently than the hour markers. The two-tone case and silver tapisserie dial is an incredible look. This watch does not come with box and papers. We do not know the service history, but it is running well.

title: Audemars Piguet Royal Oak Concept Black Panther Flying Tourbillon Full Set
description: This Audemars Piguet Royal Oak Concept Black Panther is an amazing concept Audemars Piguet Flying Tourbillon. description: A w/ Copy Service Papers The Audemars Piguet Royal Oak Offshore Chronograph Reference 26400IO.OO.A004CA is a very sporty watch with large dimensions. The watch was introduced in 2017. This watch has a very attractive grey dial with a unique internally magnified date window. This watch is powered by the automatic chronograph calibre 3126 / 3840. The watch comes with a copy of the service papers and is keeping good time.

title: Cartier Paris Tank Cintrée in 18K Yellow Gold Unpolished
description: The Cartier Tank Cintrée is one of my favorite Cartier models. The cases are very well made and among the most beautiful styles from the manufacturer. These timepieces have grown to become highly collectible over recent years. This example dates to circa 1979-1980. It features a beautiful engraving on the caseback “31 Marzo 1999 - Papa”. It features an 18K yellow gold case. The case appears to be unpolished. It features an ETA calibre 2512. It is paired on a Jean Rousseau leather strap and Cartier deployant buckle. The case measures 20mm in diameter and 36mm in length. It features a beautiful Paris dial. The watch does not come with box and papers. We do not know the service history, but it is running well.To learn more about the spectacular watches from Cartier, read our article My Dream Cartier Collection .

title: Cartier Tank Louis Xl Jumbo 17002 in 18K White Gold Unpolished
description: The Cartier Tank Louis is one of the most sophisticated dress watches and these models have grown to become highly collectible over recent years. It is a great contrast to many sports Rolex models within a collection and can be worn in both a casual and dressed up state. This example dates to the 1970s. It features an 18K white gold case which is extremely rare. These are the largest vintage Cartier Tank models. The case measures 28mm in diameter and 35mm in length. It appears to be unpolished. The dial appears to be a service dial with SWISS at 6 o'clock. It is powered by the automatic calibre 170. This is an interesting model also worn by David Prowse (the famous actor who played Darth Vader in the Stars Wars Trilogy). Prowse owned a yellow gold example from the era. The watch does not come with box and papers. We do not know the service history but it is running well. It comes with a Cartier strap that is very short. It also comes with a white-gold Cartier deployant buckle.

title: Cartier CPCP Tank à Vis Etanche Reference 2608 in 18k YG
description: This Cartier CPCP Tank à Vis Etanche reference 2608 is a special timepiece in 18k yellow gold. The watch measures 28mm in diameter by 40mm in length. It is powered by the manual wind calibre 9701MC which is beautifully decorated. This example dates to the early 2000s. It features a beautiful silver guilloche dial with painted Roman numerals. The cases appears to be unpolished and is paired on a new Cartier strap. The CPCP Tank à Vis Etanche Reference 2608 in 18k YG is of a limited run of only a few hundred pieces. title: Cartier Santos-Dumont Ref. W2SA0096 LM Lacquer Olive Green Platinum Unpolished Full Set Like New
description: This is a sophisticated Cartier Santos Dumont time only dress watch. This reference WGSA0096 features a beautiful olive sunburst dial with Arabic numerals. It features an amazing translucent olive green lacquer bezel. The watch is paired on a beautiful olive green leather strap with platinum pin buckle. The case is made of platinum and features green accents and measures approximately 32mm and is 43mm lug to lug. It features a ruby set beaded crown. Learn more about these watches within Charlie Dunne’s article ‘ Collector's Guide: Vintage Abercrombie & Fitch Seafarer Watches ’. The watch does not come with box and papers. We do not know the service history, but it is running well. title: Heuer Chronomatic Monaco Paintless Wonder Dial Reference 1133 Unpolished
description: The Heuer Monaco was introduced in 1969 with the first automatic chronograph movement, the calibre 11. Coupled by the association of Steve McQueen’s decision to wear the watch in the film ‘Le Mans’, the watch is nothing short of iconic. This example is one of the most famous Heuer Monacos on the planet (outside of the numerous Steve McQueen Le Mans models). It is one of the earliest examples known of the Heuer Monaco Chronomatic reference 1133. It is the rare variant with the “Chronomatic” font and luminous earlier hand set. The dial has developed an incredibly beautiful patina with the brass dial reacting through the blue paint - hence the nickname “Paintless Wonder” Monaco. The watch dates to circa 1969. The Heuer Monaco is actually quite a rare model and we are seeing more collectors recognize the reference 1133 as a staple within the vintage chronograph collection. This example is particularly special as it formerly belonged to the monumental vintage Heuer collector and historian, Jeff Stein. The watch was in Stein’s collection for over 18 years and was one of his most celebrated watches of all time. For those looking for one of the earliest examples of a historically important model, this is a grail watch. The case appears to be unpolished. It is stainless steel and measures approximately 38mm x 40mm. The watch does not come with a box and papers. We do not know the service history, but it is running well.

title: TAG Heuer Skipper For HODINKEE Limited Edition Unpolished Full Set
description: The Skipper is one of the many incredible Heuer watches to feature a touch of vibrant design. Drawing inspiration from the iconic reference 7754, the Skipperara would re-emerge in June 2017 when HODINKEE introduced this limited edition to great fanfare. The watch swiftly sold out and since its release, the watch remains one of the most successful limited editions from both the media company and watchmaker. The Skipper is a tremendous watch for the summer, capturing a high-spirited look on just about any strap paring. The watch is powered by the TAG Heuer caliber 18, and is on view through the sapphire exhibition caseback. The dimensions are 39mm in diameter, 11mm tall, and the lug-width is 19mm. The case is unpolished. The watch comes "full set" with box and papers. It comes with all the straps. We do not know the service history, but it is running well.

title: Heuer Chronomatic Jo Siffert Autavia Reference 1163 Unpolished
description: This Heuer “Chronomatic Siffert” Autavia reference 1163 is one of the most elusive grail chronographs from Heuer. It features a 1413XX serial. The very earliest Heuer automatic chronographs (Monaco, Autavia, and Carrera) said CHRONOMATIC on the dial above the Heuer shield and they date to 1969 with the model name appearing above 6 o’clock. The United States was the primary market for Heuer and due to the lack of customers understanding what CHRONOMATIC meant, Heuer within a month or two of beginning production changed the dials to say “AUTOMATIC CHRONOGRAPH” above 6:00 and moved the model name above the HEUER shield logo. In the last decade, only a few Jo Siffert Chronomatic models have up for sale (in addition to one prototype). These models were nicknamed after the legendary Swiss Formula One driver Jo Siffert who famously wore a CHRONOMATIC Siffert in his career and represented Heuer. Jo was a friend of Steve McQueen and inspiration for his character Michael Delaney and lent him his watch during the filming of Le Mans , although it did not end up in the movie. The case appears to be unpolished. It features an automatic movement (Caliber 11 made by Heuer-Léonidas), and is 42mm in diameter by 47mm lug to lug. It is paired on a fantastic leather rally strap and later Heuer signed buckle. The watch comes with a Gay Freres bracelet with HLD end links dated to 1969. It could benefit from tightening. The bracelet is missing one beaded section from the last end link and one from the last link near the clasp. The watch was recently serviced and is running well. The watch does not include the box and papers. This is a rare opportunity for any collector of Heuer grail watches.

title: Heuer “All-Lume” Mk 4 Autavia Reference 2446
description: The Heuer Autavia is recognized by collectors as one of the great sports chronographs of the 1960s. This reference 2446 is the 2nd execution of the reference introduced in circa 1967 with a fluid lug design, tapering down toward the wrist with thinner, beveled lugs. Along with many of its contemporaries of the era, it is powered by the Valjoux 72. The reference 2446 is regarded as one of the great Heuer racing chronographs. The present example is a rare “All-Lume” variant of the Autavia reference 2446. This is the 4th execution or MK 4 dial which is seen in the late 1960s. These models have the “H bezel” (or 12 hour bezel) and tachymeter variants. The dimensions are 38mm in diameter with a height of 13mm. The case has been polished in the past. The last example to come to market was at the Heuer Parade which achieved a result of $56,000 . It is estimated that only 8 examples are known to exist making it one of the rarest Heuers Autavias! The watch does not come with a box and papers. The service history is unknown, but it is running well.

title: Heuer Carrera Ref. 2447N Unpolished
description: The Carrera is an iconic sports chronograph which is one of the most versatile watches to have in a collection. This is a very attractive example with the black dial. The case appears to be unpolished. It measures 36 millimeters in diameter and 45mm lug-to-lug. The watch is powered by the Valjoux manual-winding calibre 72. It is paired on a aftermarket leather strap and anonymous buckle. It comes with an anonymous bracelet that looks great. The watch dates to the mid 1960s. It features the early hexagonal caseback. The watch does not come with box and papers. We do not know the service history, but it is running great.

title: Heuer Dato Carrera Reference 3147N Indianapolis Motor Speedway Indy 500
description: The Heuer Carrera is one of the legendary chronograph designs of the 20th century. Featuring stark angled lugs that were a product of the architecture of the 1960s, the present watch is notably a “first execution” and features an unpolished case. Finding Carreras from the 1960s with in great condition is extremely difficult. The reference 3147 was the first Heuer Carrera with date and this is a 3147N with the N meaning “Noir” indicating a black dial. The movement is a Landeron 189 with date and the case back is thicker on these to accommodate the thicker movement with the date. The case diameter is 36mm with a lug width of 18mm. The present example is a bit of a hodgepodge. The watch features service replacement hands with Super-LumiNova. The case has been lightly polished and it has a replacement crystal. The case back sticker is in tact. It is possible the dial was placed in the watch. Regardless, it is a very rare dial and highly coveted vintage Heuer. An Autavia model with this dial sold at Christie’s for nearly $200,000 back in 2017 . You can read more about the origins of the Carrera in the in-depth article that I wrote for HODINKEE back in 2013 . We do not know the service history, but the watch is running well. It does not come with a box or papers.

title: Universal Genève Dato-Compax Reference 22325 W/ WWII Provenance Unpolished
description: This is more than just a spectacular Universal Geneve Dato-Compax chronograph. It was Mayhew Y. "Bo" Foster's timekeeper on May 9, 1945 while he flew Hermann Göring in a Stinson L-5 Sentinel from Kitzbuhel, Austria to Augsburg, Germany for interrogation by the 7th Army before he later stood trial at Nuremberg. “Bo" Foster (October 9, 1911 – March 21, 2011) was a decorated American pilot and hero. Foster graduated in 1937 with a degree in English from Yale. For his actions in World War II - including 70 reconnaissance combat missions - Foster was awarded the Silver Star for his service in France in 1944, the Air Medal, and the Légion d'Honneur for his contribution to liberating France. Foster later reached the rank of Brigadier General in the Montana Army National Guard Foster transported Göring in the L-5, a larger plane than the L-4 he normally piloted, because Göring weighed more than 300 pounds. In a letter to his wife, Virginia, written at the time, Foster described his first impression of Göring as "effeminate [and he] gave me the creeps . . . Several times I had the impulse to turn the plane over and see if I could shake him out, but he was wedged in like a champagne cork… He acted as though he was going on a sightseeing tour, or really as though I was going on a sightseeing tour, and he was showing me where he grew up. I had a .45 in a shoulder holster, but he couldn't reach that. But neither could I, because I had two hands controlling the plane.” When Foster arrived, there was just a single jeep at the airstrip to meet the arriving flight. Foster rode with Göring and formally turned him over to the intelligence officer without ceremony. It seems likely that Göring was also wearing a Universal Geneve chronograph in steel on that flight - in his case an oversized non-luminous Compax reference 22430 that was in his possession at Nuremberg and sold at auction in 2016. DJ Hurricane has also worked with many of the legendary Hip hop artists including Kool G Rap, Public Enemy, Flipmode Squad, Rah Digga, Xzibit, Pharoahe Monch, Tick Daddy, Coolio, Talib Kweli, Papoose, Sen-Dog. In 2024, DJ Hurricane was inducted into the Long Island Music and Entertainment Hall of Fame . An awesome part of Hurricane’s resume was that he worked as security for Run D.M.C. during the Raising Hell Tour. The case measures approximately 46mm in diameter. The bracelet will fit a wrist over 7.5 inches in circumference. The watch was purchased new in 2002 by DJ Hurricane. In 2008, he had the watch customized by Jacob & Co. to feature a diamond set case. We do not know the service history, but the watch is running well. It comes with box and papers. The card is not filled out which is common for this era. The watch comes with a letter of provenance.

title: OMEGA Speedmaster Racing Dial Ref. 145.022-69 ST Full Set w/ Extract
description: A Speedmaster Racing Dial Ref. 145.022-69 ST Full Set w/ Extract The OMEGA Speedmaster is certainly one of the most iconic watches with a truly rich history of exploration and sport. This is an incredible “Racing Dial” reference 145.022-69. The watch was originally delivered to Japan in 1971 and was sold in 1975 according to the papers. The racing dial is one of the most exciting and interesting dial variants on any Speedy. These models are very rare and this example is in awesome condition. The dial is incredibly attractive. title: OMEGA Speedmaster Reference 145.022-69 BA In 18K YG
description: A Speedmaster Reference 145.022-69 BA in 18K YG OMEGA introduced the Speedmaster in 1957, initially created for drivers in automotive racing needing to time their laps. However, the Speedmaster would reach eternal iconic status by eventually being qualified for spaceflight by NASA after an intense testing of several of the highest-grade chronographs of the 1960s. NASA selected the Speedmaster as the exclusive watch for use by its astronauts. The OMEGA Speedmaster reference 145.022-69 BA was the first OMEGA Speedmaster to be produced in 18k yellow gold. Only 30 examples were produced in total for astronauts and two were produced for President Nixon and Vice President Agnew. The next examples were given to Astronauts and are considered by many to be the grail OMEGA Speedmasters. On October 20, 2022, Wally Schirra’s personal OMEGA Speedmaster Professional BA 145.022 was sold for $1,906,954 . This example is one that was sold to the public. The 18K yellow-gold case is in has been lightly polshed. The dial is fantastic and the bezel remains in good condition. The watch is powered by the caliber 861. The bracelet is long and should fit a wrist approximately 7.1 inches. Finding an example with a long bracelet is incredibly difficult. For those looking for an epic gold Speedmaster, these are amazing watches. To learn more about the OMEGA Speedmaster, you can watch my ‘Reference Points: Understanding The Entire Lineage Of The OMEGA Speedmaster ’ video and read the corresponding article. The watch was sold in Phillips: START-STOP-RESET: 88 Epic Stainless Steel Chronographs in 2016 for over $54,777, and later in the thematic DOUBLE SIGNED auction in 2019 . title: Heuer Carrera Transitional Dial Reference 2447NST Unpolished
description: The Heuer Carrera is one of the legendary chronograph designs of the 20th century. Featuring stark angled lugs that were a product of the architecture of the 1960s. You can read more about the origins of the Carrera in the in-depth article that I wrote back in 2013 . This example is the extremely rare reference 2447 NST ( N oir/Black dial, S ilver/White Registers, and T achymeter) - However, with a transitional dial that is possibly unique. This is the only example known to the collector community. Legendary vintage Heuer collector/expert (and fan of Charlie Dunne) Jeff Stein has blessed it as the only known transitional. The dial features the second execution dial configuration with a first execution tachymeter scale - solid-metal hour markers with enlarged tachymeter numerals. This tachymeter scale/format is seen in the first execution 2447T with red demarcations (the earliest tachymeter-dial Carrera). It features a slightly more grey dial than the “standard” 2447NST. It is a phenomenal watch and one of the most attractive inverse panda watches ever. The watch is powered by the manual-wind Valjoux calibre 72. The case appears to be unpolished. The case measures approximately 35.5mm in diameter. The watch comes from an American collector that Charlie likes. Good Provenance! It has been in his collection for several years. The watch does not come with box and papers. We do not know the service history, but it is running well. It is paired on a aftermarket rally strap and buckle.
